pr_comments:
Thanks to @jc-kynesim for the patch.

Report from original bug reporter (@HiassofT)

> thanks a lot, your EAC3 patch worked fine here! :+1:
The Dolby sample worked here, too, and the 3 Hobbit files with EAC3 audio tracks I fount in my archive worked fine, too (all of them "stuttered" before)
have been testing this change the other day and it fixed the issue for me. A big thanks to everybody involved.

I've made some formatting changes to meet the current code style. The diffs are available in the following links:
 - [PR23217-0001-4e218fdda7-AEStreamInfo-Support-EAC3-independ.diff](https://jenkins.kodi.tv/job/BuildMulti-PR/26459/artifact/PR23217-0001-4e218fdda7-AEStreamInfo-Support-EAC3-independ.diff)

For more information please see our [current code style guidelines](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/docs/CODE_GUIDELINES.md).

I think that would be a worse solution.
The code added is basically very similar to the code in the other branch of the if.
Keeping it similar makes it easier to spot this.
Having a mixture of two coding styles in one function is going to be worse.
The final result of this PR fixes the bug and fixes the coding style of the whole file.

@thexai Would it but OK by you if the patch sequence went - update entire file to new coding style and then apply patch in the new coding style (rather then the other way round which is how it is at the moment)? I have to agree with @popcornmix that mixing styles within a function is truly horrid.

> @thexai Would it but OK by you if the patch sequence went - update entire file to new coding style and then apply patch in the new coding style (rather then the other way round which is how it is at the moment)? I have to agree with @popcornmix that mixing styles within a function is truly horrid.

Yes it's generally considered ok to run clang-format on an entire section (or file) and commit that prior to making the actual changes/commits. This is typically done to help clarify the code changes that are contained in a commit to avoid bloating it with formatting changes.

This does typically make it harder to backport but it's not impossible either.

In this case the code change is easy to read so I don't really think that formatting the entire file is needed. I'm not opposed to it though if it is causing others grief to mix styles in a single file.

> Would it but OK by you if the patch sequence went - update entire file to new coding style and then apply patch in the new coding style (rather then the other way round which is how it is at the moment)?

Yes, that would be correct. Then the new code added would already be with the new style and the Jenkins message will disappear.

Although it is not necessary to change the entire file, just the new code added.

I've noticed on webOS these streams are unfortunately still broken. It seems that some `m_info` variables would also need to be updated with the information of the dependent stream. Right now `m_channels` and `m_ac3FrameSize` is only parsed from the main stream thus giving only 4 channels on a 7.1 stream.

Ah! very believable - I did worry about that - but as I don't know that code well and what I did seemed to work on the test cases and platform I had I left it as was. If you've got a test case & platform that shows the problem then patch away.  Or if you can make it fail on arm/linux then I'll happily build a new patch.
I guess it's not relevant on all other platforms except for webOS as they don't need correct information on the channel count for passthrough.
If you want I can make a best guess at a patch but without a test case it will just be a guess.

issue_context.title: Garbled sound with DD+/EAC3 passthrough and official Dolby DD+ 7.1 sample
issue_context.body:
## Bug report
### Describe the bug
When playing the Dolby Digital Plus 7.1 sample file [MP4_HPL40_30fps_channel_id_71.mp4](http://media.developer.dolby.com/DDP/MP4_HPL40_30fps_channel_id_71.mp4) from the [Dolby website](https://developer.dolby.com/tools-media/sample-media/video-streams/hd-video-streams/) audio output is garbled - it sounds like sound on/off in quick succession or stuttering - and kodi logs tons of "large audio sync error"s.

## Expected Behavior
Kodi is able to pass through official Dolby samples.

### Debuglog
The debuglog can be found here: http://ix.io/2OvU

## Additional context or screenshots (if appropriate)
The 5.1 DD+ sample [MP4_HPL40_30fps_channel_id_51.mp4](http://media.developer.dolby.com/DDP/MP4_HPL40_30fps_channel_id_51.mp4) from the webpage plays fine with passthrough enabled.

When disabling DD+/EAC3 passthrough the 7.1 sample plays fine with software decode (tested with downmix to 2.0)

### Your Environment
Used Operating system:
 - [X] Linux
 - Operating system version/name: LibreELEC master, RPi4
 - Kodi version: master, githash 1e6f7347ec56233923d176825f0ccdc6a60d76d3

Edit: Kodi must support dependent frames or it could not support 7.1 EAC3.

The sample seems to have this frame ordering:
EAC3 Frame - 920byte
EAC3 dependent Frame - 616byte

Most other EAC3 streams I see are with AC3 + EAC3 dependent Frame (Bluray / Streaming) or EAC3 Frame only (HDDVD). This file is effectively a 7.1 EAC3 file with no AC3 backward compatibility.

I think I can see the problem. Kodi only checks for an EAC3 extension frame if the first frame is legacy AC3 (BSID <= 10):
https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/49a04cd6a7f49ea9a0f05c492b11a3ba7c542a99/xbmc/cores/AudioEngine/Utils/AEStreamInfo.cpp#L373

Things are not so easy. The raw stuff needs to be packed in so called IEC frames. Whenever the parsing of the raw payload fails, e.g. no sync on them, packing fails and signal is lost. The issue at hand is a problem with kodi`s syncer and packer. You can check if android does it properly by switching over to Android packer as the audio device.
